source.paper: Craig A. Tovey, A simplified NP-complete satisfiability problem, Discrete Applied Mathematics 8 (1984), Theorem 2.1
source.construction: If an original variable x appears k times, introduce x_1,...,x_k, replace the i-th original occurrence by x_i with the inherited sign, and append the cyclic 2-clauses (x_i OR NOT x_{i+1}) for i=1,...,k with indices modulo k.
source.occurrence_bound: Each copy x_i appears exactly once in an inherited original clause and exactly twice in the link cycle, hence at most three times overall.

carrier_view.witness_selection: Choose exactly one literal occurrence from every clause. A selection is conflict-free when it never selects both signs of the same copy variable.
carrier_view.link_choice_bit: For the link clause C_i=(x_i OR NOT x_{i+1}), let y_i=1 when its selected witness is x_i and y_i=0 when its selected witness is NOT x_{i+1}.

theorem.name: TOVEY_LINK_CYCLE_COLLAPSES_TO_ONE_GLOBAL_SIGN
theorem.statement: For every copy cycle of one original variable, every conflict-free one-witness-per-link-clause selection has y_1=...=y_k. Consequently, after existentially eliminating all link-clause witnesses, the normalized occurrence carrier enforces exactly the original global sign-consistency relation on the inherited occurrences and nothing weaker.
proof: Copy x_i receives a positive selected link witness exactly when y_i=1, from C_i.
The same copy x_i receives a negative selected link witness exactly when y_{i-1}=0, from C_{i-1}.
Conflict-freeness therefore forbids y_i=1 together with y_{i-1}=0, equivalently y_i <= y_{i-1} for every i on the directed cycle.
Chaining the cyclic inequalities gives y_1<=y_k<=...<=y_1, hence all y_i are equal.

If all y_i=1, every copy has a positive selected link occurrence, so any selected inherited occurrence of that copy must also be positive. If all y_i=0, every copy has a negative selected link occurrence, so any selected inherited occurrence must be negative.

Conversely, if all selected inherited occurrences of the original variable have one common sign (or none are selected), choose all y_i to that sign; then every link clause has one selected witness and no copy sees both signs.
Thus eliminating the entire link cycle recovers exactly the original relation: selected inherited witnesses for x may be empty or may use only one of the two signs.

corollary.name: TOVEY_NORMALIZATION_IS_EXACT_FANOUT_REALIZATION_NOT_TRACTABILITY_GAIN
corollary.statement: In the P3-overlap / read-2 witness carrier, the Tovey link cycles can be eliminated exactly in polynomial time, but the result is the original arbitrary-variable sign-consistency constraint. Therefore the cycle topology does not by itself yield a smaller universal state space, a bounded-width decomposition, or a new polynomial augmenting-path theorem.
corollary.anti_loop: Do not claim that the link cycles make the hard carrier easy merely because each copy has local degree three or because each equality gadget is a directed cycle. Exact elimination returns the pre-normalization fanout problem.

next_target.name: E8_CLAUSE_RANK3_DETERMINANT_COEFFICIENT_OR_GLOBAL_CANCELLATION_V2_7
next_target.directive: Work after source-return on a representation that attacks global clause choice directly. In the local determinant carrier Q(L,M,R)=1+L+M+R+LR, each literal occurrence is a rank-one matrix atom. Aggregating all occurrences of one clause under one clause variable produces a rank-at-most-three update. Rank-one clause updates collapse by the matrix determinant lemma; the live obligation is an exact polynomial mechanism for the rank-two/rank-three aggregation without enumerating one occurrence per clause.
